findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow has no state machine; mark_sent can be called at any time with no guard against re-sending or sending before validation. The struct exposes raw lifecycle booleans that let callers reach invalid state combinations like is_sent=true with status="pending".
findings.failure_mode: invalid state reachable: callers can set is_sent=true while status remains "pending", creating logically inconsistent leases that break downstream contracts
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single LeaseStatus enum typestate that encodes valid transitions (e.g., Created -> Validated -> Sent) so illegal transitions are compile-time errors

findings.problem: status: String allows any string value including "sent", "pending", "foo", "". mark_sent assigns a hardcoded string literal directly, bypassing any validation. This violates the law that domain APIs should not expose raw primitives.
findings.failure_mode: caller passes status: String with any arbitrary value; no invariant enforcement at the type level; domain invariants rely entirely on convention
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a `LeaseStatus` enum (e.g., `enum LeaseStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }`) so the only valid status values are the enum variants

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a lifecycle boolean that should be a typestate transition. It is independent of is_sent: bool, so both can be true or both false simultaneously with no ordering enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: lease can have is_validated=true and is_sent=false (sent before validated) or both true without ever having gone through a proper transition, breaking audit trail
findings.fix: Remove both `is_validated` and `is_sent` booleans. Replace with a single typestate enum that encodes the valid lifecycle ordering (Created -> Validated -> Sent)

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an optional lifecycle field stored as a separate Option. It can be Some(t) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true — inconsistent combinations that the type system cannot prevent.
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(timestamp) with is_sent=false (timestamp recorded but lease not marked sent) or None with is_sent=true (sent but no timestamp), breaking time-based auditing
findings.fix: Move timestamp into the typestate enum variant that owns it, e.g. `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`, so the timestamp co-occurs with the sent state by construction

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive for a domain identifier. Any string value including empty, whitespace-only, or malformed IDs can be constructed without validation. No newtype guards the lease ID.
findings.failure_mode: callers can create a LeaseWorkflow with id="", id="  ", or id="not-a-real-id"; no domain-level validation on identifiers; string equality is the only identity check
findings.fix: Replace `id: String` with a `LeaseId` newtype constructed via a fallible smart constructor (e.g., `impl LeaseId { fn new(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> }`)

findings.problem: raw primitives (String for id, String for status, bools for lifecycle, Option<u64> for timestamp) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. Callers can construct invalid LeaseWorkflow domain states directly with `LeaseWorkflow { id: "", status: "banana", is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }`. There is no parse boundary at all — no smart constructor, no validation, no typed errors.
findings.failure_mode: invalid domain states are constructible at the call site with zero validation; the entire module accepts hostile inputs as valid domain values
findings.fix: Add a `LeaseWorkflow::try_new` smart constructor or derive from parsed DTOs at the boundary with fallible smart constructors for id, status, and lifecycle; expose only the validated typestate enum as the public domain API
